subject.title: feat: 0.5.0 API surface — archive policy, publication mechanics, sync locks, secret create-only, Root.walk, cleanup receipts

question: Should version 0.5 intentionally retire execution of configured Python helpers, retain only the documented 0.5.x warning-and-mapping bridge, and make require mode depend on an installed native platform binding?
rationale: The branch is internally consistent and evidence-backed, but this changes the upgrade contract for existing deployments and couples the public API rollout to a new multi-package native release process; repository maintainers must choose that product and release direction.

options.title: Approve the 0.5 native transition
options.body: Adopt the documented native-only helper contract, publish all platform packages through the trusted release workflow, and remove the migration aliases in 0.6 as described.

options.title: Preserve Python execution longer
options.body: Keep an explicit, documented Python compatibility path beyond 0.5, which reduces upgrade breakage but retains the prior process-execution boundary and maintenance burden.

options.title: Stage native APIs separately
options.body: Land non-native public helpers first and defer the native package/release transition to a separately approved versioned rollout.

recommendation.title: Approve the 0.5 native transition
recommendation.body: Adopt the documented native-only helper contract, publish all platform packages through the trusted release workflow, and remove the migration aliases in 0.6 as described.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history and final discussion show the clearest available ownership of the proposed native transition and its release mechanics.
